Simple: The non-aggression principle advocated by libertarians is an insane and unworkable idea. I don't concern myself with absolutes in ideology, instead concentrating on things that can work in reality. So, for example: property rights. Nope, not absolute. Taxation is something we need to function as a society, and always has been. It allows for the distribution of effort in such a way as to allow for society to exist. Without it, each individual cannot assume that there will be resources to handle the bits they can't handle, so they have to handle all of it. For example: I can't count on my home being defended unless there is a professional military and police force. If those things are absent, I need to devote at least some of my personal resources to the defence of my home, and probably a large amount of resources (especially if we also remove social safety nets).

Now, let's talk in realistic terms about social safety nets, or social welfare. I have personally been homeless. Yes, it sucked, and yes, I was able to overcome it and am now educated and gainfully employed. I did this without access to welfare - great, I'm a libertarian hero. Well, not quite. I did have some assistance, see, I live in a country where we have free health care, and where we subsidize post-secondary education. I took advantage of both of these things while homeless, and without them I probably would have died homeless. Now, have in my lifetime been a net contributor to society? Yep, absolutely. I have increased the overall prosperity of my country with my efforts. I have worked in the IT sector for twenty years, and have been responsible for some major productivity gains for multiple companies. That happens to end up being true of the vast majority of people who are on welfare at some point in their lives. Also, during my time without welfare I did steal, I did deal drugs, I did commit acts of violence. I was not a good actor in society. Had welfare been more accessible during that time I would have been unlikely to commit the criminal acts I did commit (you would be amazed what you are willing to do when you don't have food).

You can break rights down into groups - and you can do it without using the NAP. For example: the right to use land can actually be viewed as a common right, as land is a common good for everyone. Your personal use of that land can then be restricted in some ways that make sense. Many cultures actually do this, allowing for things like leaving a field fallow for a year, but with caveats that land you don't use reverts to the common usage. Now, your bodily autonomy is a different thing entirely. You are the sole owner of your body, therefor you are allowed to put anything you want into it. You have a right to have it not interfered with, and the only exception to that autonomy is someone else's bodily autonomy.

There is much more, but a lot of it boils down to the idea that the NAP as espoused by libertarians doesn't work. It fails every test of sanity and functionality you can throw at.
